_about: Curated F-16 store reference for the Wizzo. Weights and missile ranges are read live from Falcon4_WCD.xml; this file supplies the employment guidance, delivery profiles, fuzing and laser-code applicability that the game files do not contain. Figures are BMS-practical reference values drawn from the BMS manuals and standard Viper procedures -- treat them as planning guidance, not as certified release tables.

rules: Remaining three digits are each 1-8. A 0 or 9 in any position is invalid.
The code set on the weapon must match the code set on the targeting pod.
Set codes in the DTC or the loadout screen before stepping; verify on the TGP LASER page.
A buddy-lasing flight must be told your code -- it is not shared automatically.

stores.guidance: Active radar, inertial midcourse then autonomous terminal
employment: Launch high and fast -- range scales strongly with launch altitude and Mach. A shot from 30k/0.9M reaches far further than the same shot from 10k.
Read the DLZ on the MFD: Raero is the kinematic limit, Ropt the optimal shot, Rtr the range from which a target that turns and runs can still be killed.
Shots taken beyond Rtr are easily defeated. Rtr or closer is where kills come from.
Support the shot until the missile goes active (pitbull), then you are free to manoeuvre. The MFD counts down time to active.
Respect MAR -- inside minimum abort range you cannot turn away before the threat's own shot arrives.
TWS lets you shoot multiple targets but drops track more readily than RWS single-target-track.
stores.fuzing: Not applicable -- proximity/impact, no aircrew setting.

employment: All-aspect with a wide off-boresight capability -- it will take shots well outside the HUD field of view.
Slave the seeker with the radar or cue it uncaged; uncage before launch so the seeker tracks the target rather than the boresight.
Best results inside 5 nm. Long-range IR shots bleed energy and are easily defeated by a turn.
Watch for sun and flares in the seeker's field of view during terminal guidance.
stores.fuzing: Not applicable -- proximity/impact.

employment: All-aspect on the L and M, but the rear quarter remains by far the highest-probability shot.
Uncage the seeker before launch and listen for the growl to confirm a good lock.
Practical envelope is roughly 1-5 nm. Do not waste shots at the outer limit.
Older P and J variants are effectively rear-aspect only.
stores.fuzing: Not applicable -- proximity/impact.

employment: Block 40/50 carries roughly 510 rounds at about 6000 rounds per minute -- five seconds of total trigger time.
Air-to-air: use the EEGS funnel, fire in short bursts inside 1 nm.
Strafe: 10-15 degree dive, open fire around 4000 ft slant, break off by 2000 ft to stay clear of your own ricochets and debris.
The gun cross is not the aiming point -- fly the CCIP or funnel solution.
stores.fuzing: PGU-28 combined effects / M56 HEI depending on load.

employment: CCIP for visual dive deliveries, CCRP for level or blind release against a steerpoint or TGP mark.
A 30-45 degree dive release from 8-12k ft AGL gives good accuracy with adequate frag separation.
Level low-altitude releases with low-drag bombs are hazardous -- you fly through your own frag pattern. Keep releases above roughly 5000 ft AGL or use a retarded variant.
Accuracy is very sensitive to release conditions -- wings level, steady G and on-speed at release.
Ripple pairs to cover an area target rather than aiming single bombs at each aimpoint.
stores.fuzing: FMU-139 nose/tail. Set arming delay on the SMS -- longer delays for penetration, shorter for surface burst.

employment: The retarder opens after release and steepens the fall, letting you release low and still escape the frag pattern.
Intended for low-level laydown deliveries -- 300-500 ft AGL passes are practical.
Confirm the SMS is set to the retarded profile, otherwise the CCIP solution uses the wrong ballistics and the bombs fall long.
Retarded bombs are far less accurate from medium altitude -- use low-drag or guided stores from height.
stores.fuzing: FMU-139 with retarded arming. Ballute or fins must be armed for the retarded profile to work.

employment: Release into the bomb's glide envelope, then lase continuously through impact. Stopping the laser early leaves the bomb ballistic.
Typical medium-altitude delivery: release from 15-20k ft in a shallow dive or level, 4-8 nm slant range.
Begin lasing roughly 8-12 seconds before impact. Lasing too early bleeds energy as the bomb chases the spot and can cause it to fall short.
Keep the target within the pod's field of regard through impact -- do not turn the pod off target while the bomb is in flight.
Paveway II uses bang-bang control -- it corrects in full deflections and loses energy quickly. Do not release short and expect it to reach.
Weather matters: cloud, smoke and dust between pod and target will break the laser and the bomb will miss.
stores.fuzing: FMU-139 or FMU-152. Instantaneous for soft targets, delayed for structures.
stores.laser_note: Laser code must match the targeting pod. Default 1688; valid 1111-1788 with digits 2-4 in the 1-8 range.
requires: Targeting pod (or a buddy lasing on your code)

employment: Paveway III flies a proportional, energy-efficient profile and reaches considerably further than Paveway II.
Supports both low-altitude and medium-altitude deliveries, but the release envelope is narrow -- respect the LAR cue.
Lase continuously through impact as with any LGB.
The penetrating warheads on the GBU-24A, -27 and -28 need a steep terminal angle to work. A shallow impact wastes the weapon on a hardened target.
Long time of flight -- plan to stay pointed in and lasing for a considerable run-in.
stores.fuzing: FMU-143 / FMU-152 with delay for penetration before detonation.
stores.laser_note: Laser code must match the targeting pod. Default 1688; valid 1111-1788.
requires: Targeting pod (or a buddy lasing on your code)

stores.guidance: GPS with inertial backup -- no laser, no lasing required
stores.role: All-weather precision attack on fixed coordinates
employment: Fire and forget. Once released you may turn away immediately -- no laser, no pod, no support required.
Accuracy depends entirely on target coordinate quality. Verify the steerpoint or TGP-derived coordinates before release.
Release inside the LAR cue on the MFD. From 20-25k ft the weapon reaches roughly 12-15 nm.
Genuinely all-weather -- cloud between you and the target does not matter, unlike an LGB.
The (v)1 and (v)2 use blast-fragmentation warheads for soft and area targets; the (v)3 and (v)4 use BLU-109 penetrators for hardened targets.
Set the impact azimuth and angle in the SMS when attacking a target where the approach geometry matters, such as a runway or a bunker face.
stores.fuzing: FMU-152 programmable. Set arming delay and, where required, function delay before release.

employment: Can be employed as a pure GPS weapon against fixed coordinates, or with terminal laser guidance against a moving target.
Laser mode is what makes this weapon worth carrying against vehicles -- GPS alone cannot hit something that drives away.
In laser mode, lase through impact exactly as with a conventional LGB.
Confirm the intended mode in the SMS before release -- the delivery profile differs between GPS and laser employment.
stores.fuzing: FMU-152 programmable.
stores.laser_note: Laser code applies when employed in laser mode and must match the pod. Default 1688.

stores.role: Standoff precision attack, many targets per pass
employment: Four weapons per pylon -- exceptional magazine depth for multiple aimpoints in one pass.
Deployable wings give roughly 40 nm of glide from high altitude. Release high and fast for maximum reach.
Small warhead with a focused blast -- excellent against soft point targets, insufficient against heavy structures.
Assign a distinct aimpoint to each weapon before release rather than rippling them at one target.
stores.fuzing: Programmable electronic fuze; airburst, impact or delay.

stores.role: Area attack on soft targets, vehicles and personnel
employment: The dispenser opens at a set height of function and spreads submunitions over a footprint -- you are aiming a pattern, not a point.
Height of function controls the footprint: lower HOF means a tighter, denser pattern, higher HOF means a wider, thinner one.
Set both HOF and burst spin (RN) on the SMS before release. Wrong settings scatter the load uselessly.
Release from medium altitude in a shallow dive. Wind drift across the footprint is significant.
Ineffective against armour and hardened targets -- use these on trucks, guns, SAM sites and troops.
stores.fuzing: FZU-39 proximity sets the height of function. Set HOF and RN on the SMS.

stores.guidance: Ballistic dispenser with self-guiding skeet submunitions
employment: The skeet submunitions detect vehicles individually and fire downward at the hottest part of each -- purpose-built armour killer.
One weapon can disable multiple vehicles in a column.
Requires a dispersed vehicle target. Wasted on infantry, buildings or empty ground.
The CBU-105 adds WCMD wind correction and is markedly more accurate from altitude than the unguided CBU-97.
stores.fuzing: Set height of function on the SMS; the submunitions then work autonomously.

stores.guidance: Inertial tail kit with wind correction
stores.role: Accurate area attack from medium/high altitude
employment: The WCMD tail kit corrects for the wind drift that ruins unguided cluster accuracy, so this can be released from high altitude above light defences.
Still a footprint weapon -- height of function governs the pattern exactly as with an unguided dispenser.
Preferred over the CBU-87 whenever the threat picture forces a medium- or high-altitude release.
stores.fuzing: Programmable height of function via the tail kit; set on the SMS.

stores.guidance: Imaging infrared (D/G) or electro-optical (A/B), lock before launch
stores.role: Precision attack on vehicles, hardened points and ships
employment: Power the seeker up early -- the IIR variants need roughly three minutes of cooling before they will track.
Lock the target before launch. This is a fire-and-forget weapon once locked, so you can turn away immediately.
Handing off from the targeting pod to the missile seeker is much faster than hunting for the target on the narrow Maverick display.
Practical launch range is 6-10 nm from medium altitude; the seeker must be able to resolve the target to lock it.
The D has a shaped-charge warhead sized for vehicles; the G carries a much heavier blast-fragmentation warhead for structures and ships.
Boresight the seeker before employment or the first lock attempt will be off.
stores.fuzing: Impact; no aircrew setting.

stores.role: Precision attack, including designation by another party
employment: Guides on a laser spot rather than an image, so it can be employed against targets the seeker could not otherwise resolve.
Well suited to buddy lasing and to forward air controller designation -- but every party must agree the code.
Lase from before launch through impact.
Confirm the code on the missile matches the designating pod before you commit to the pass.
stores.fuzing: Impact.
stores.laser_note: Laser code must match the designating pod, whether your own or a buddy's. Default 1688.
requires: Targeting pod or an external designator

stores.role: Suppression and destruction of enemy air defences
employment: Homes on radar emissions. If the emitter shuts down before impact the missile goes ballistic, though the shutdown itself has already suppressed the site.
POS mode attacks a known threat position from the DTC or a steerpoint -- the long-range, pre-planned shot.
HAS mode uses the missile's own seeker to find and attack whatever is radiating, for reactive self-protection.
With the HTS pod the HAD page gives a far better threat picture and enables precise handoffs.
Loft the shot from high altitude and high speed for maximum reach -- range falls off sharply down low.
Fire and forget. Turn away immediately after launch rather than pressing into the threat ring.
stores.fuzing: Proximity/impact; no aircrew setting.
requires: HTS pod for HAD targeting (POS mode works without it)

stores.role: Attack on defended targets from outside the threat ring
employment: Unpowered glide weapon -- release altitude and speed directly set the range achieved. High and fast is essential.
Roughly 40 nm from high altitude, far less from low level.
Fire and forget on GPS coordinates. Verify target coordinates before release.
The JSOW-A dispenses BLU-97 submunitions over an area target; the JSOW-C is a unitary penetrator for a point target.
Long time of flight -- account for it when sequencing attacks with other package elements.
stores.fuzing: Programmable; submunition dispense altitude on the A, penetrator delay on the C.

employment: Long-range fire-and-forget weapon launched from well outside the target's defences.
The Harpoon flies a sea-skimming profile and uses its own active radar terminally -- provide a target position and launch.
Very long time of flight; deconflict with other package elements and friendly shipping before firing.
Confirm target identity before release. These weapons are launched far beyond visual range and cannot be recalled.
stores.fuzing: Impact/delayed penetration.

employment: Unguided and highly dispersed -- an area weapon, not a precision one.
Shallow dive, fire in salvos, expect a wide pattern.
White phosphorus variants are for marking targets rather than destroying them.
Firing requires closing well inside most short-range air defences. Consider the threat before committing.
stores.fuzing: Fixed by rocket type.

employment: Jams threat radars to degrade their track quality and delay or spoil their shots.
Must be switched on to have any effect -- confirm the pod is powered and in the correct mode before entering the threat area.
Jamming can also make you conspicuous. Some crews leave it in standby until spiked.
Does not make you invisible. It buys time and degrades solutions; it does not replace defensive manoeuvring and chaff.
stores.fuzing: n/a

stores.role: Target identification, designation and laser designation
employment: Required for every laser-guided weapon you intend to self-designate.
Set and verify the laser code on the pod's LASER page -- it must match the weapon's code.
Use point track for fixed targets and area track for moving ones.
Slave the pod to a steerpoint to find the target area quickly, then refine manually.
The pod is also the best identification sensor you have -- use it to confirm the target before release, especially under restrictive rules of engagement.
stores.fuzing: n/a
stores.laser_note: This pod sets the designating code. Everything you lase uses it -- confirm it matches your weapons and any buddy-lasing agreement.

employment: Detects, classifies and ranges radar emitters, driving the HAD page.
Enables precise HARM handoffs and greatly improves situational awareness against air defences.
Without it you are limited to pre-planned POS shots and reactive HAS shots.
stores.fuzing: n/a

employment: Feed and monitor the tanks -- confirm they are transferring rather than trapped, or you are carrying dead weight.
Tanks impose a drag penalty and restrict the manoeuvring envelope. Know the G limit for your configuration.
Plan to jettison before a serious engagement if fuel state allows. Empty tanks are pure drag.
Two 370 gallon wing tanks are the standard Viper configuration for anything beyond a local sortie.
stores.fuzing: n/a
